subject: English
topic: Voice Change — Active and Passive Voice (Set W7)

questions.stem:
Choose the correct PASSIVE form of the sentence:
'The teacher teaches the students every day.'

options.option_text: The students were taught by the teacher every day.
The students are taught by the teacher every day.
The students have been taught by the teacher every day.
The students are being taught by the teacher every day.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Simple present active → Simple present passive. Formula: Object + am/is/are + past participle + by + Subject. 'The teacher teaches' (Simple Present) → 'are taught'. Option A uses past tense (were). Option D uses present continuous passive (are being).

questions.stem:
Choose the correct PASSIVE form:
'She sang a beautiful song.'

options.option_text: A beautiful song was being sung by her.
A beautiful song has been sung by her.
A beautiful song was sung by her.
A beautiful song is sung by her.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Simple past active → Simple past passive. Formula: Object + was/were + past participle + by + Subject. 'Sang' (simple past) → 'was sung'. Subject 'she' becomes 'her' (object pronoun) in passive. Pronoun change: I→me, he→him, she→her, they→them, we→us.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct PASSIVE form:
'They are building a new bridge.'

options.option_text: A new bridge is being built by them.
A new bridge was being built by them.
A new bridge is built by them.
A new bridge has been built by them.

questions.explanation: A is correct. Present continuous active → Present continuous passive. Formula: Object + am/is/are + being + past participle + by + Subject. 'are building' → 'is being built'. Option B uses 'was' (past). Option C uses simple present (is built). Option D uses present perfect.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct PASSIVE form:
'He has written three novels.'

options.option_text: Three novels are written by him.
Three novels were written by him.
Three novels had been written by him.
Three novels have been written by him.

questions.explanation: D is correct. Present perfect active → Present perfect passive. Formula: Object + has/have + been + past participle + by + Subject. 'He has written' → 'have been written' (subject = three novels → plural → 'have'). Option A uses simple present. Option C uses past perfect (had been).

questions.stem:
Choose the correct PASSIVE form:
'Will she complete the project by Friday?'

options.option_text: Shall the project be completed by her by Friday?
Will the project be completed by her by Friday?
Will the project have been completed by her by Friday?
Would the project be completed by her by Friday?

questions.explanation: B is correct. Future simple question (active) → Future simple passive question. Formula: Will + Object + be + past participle + by + Subject? 'Will she complete' → 'Will...be completed by her'. 'She' changes to 'her'. Option A wrongly uses 'shall'. Option C uses future perfect passive.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct PASSIVE form (agent omitted when unknown):
'Someone broke into the house last night.'

options.option_text: The house was broken into last night.
The house was broken last night by someone.
The house is broken into last night.
Into the house was broken last night.

questions.explanation: A is correct. When the agent is unknown ('someone'), the 'by + agent' phrase is omitted. Phrasal verb 'broke into' → 'was broken into' (the preposition 'into' stays with the verb and cannot be separated). 'The house was broken into' is correct. Option B wrongly includes 'by someone'. Option D wrongly places 'into' at the front.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct PASSIVE form:
'The police arrested the thief.'

options.option_text: The thief has been arrested by the police.
The thief is arrested by the police.
The thief was being arrested by the police.
The thief was arrested by the police.

questions.explanation: D is correct. Simple past active → Simple past passive. 'Arrested' (simple past) → 'was arrested'. The police → by the police. 'The thief was arrested by the police.' Option A (has been) = present perfect. Option C (was being) = past continuous passive.

questions.stem:
Convert the PASSIVE sentence to ACTIVE:
'The match was being played when it started raining.'

options.option_text: Someone played the match when it started raining.
The players have been playing the match when it started raining.
They played the match when it started raining.
They were playing the match when it started raining.

questions.explanation: D is correct. Past continuous passive ('was being played') → Past continuous active ('were playing'). When no agent is stated in passive, use 'they' as the unnamed subject. 'Was being played' = past continuous passive → 'were playing' = past continuous active.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct PASSIVE form of the IMPERATIVE sentence:
'Shut the door.'

options.option_text: The door should be shut.
Let the door be shut.
The door must be shut.
The door was shut.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Imperative sentence (command) passive: 'Let + object + be + past participle.' 'Shut the door' → 'Let the door be shut.' This is the standard passive form for commands in English. Option A (should be) and C (must be) change the meaning to obligation/recommendation — not the pure passive of a command.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct PASSIVE form (impersonal passive):
'People say that she is very honest.'

options.option_text: It is said that she is very honest.
She is said to be very honest.
Both A and B are correct passive forms.
She was said to be very honest.

questions.explanation: C is correct. For 'People say that + clause', there are TWO standard passive forms: (1) 'It is said that she is honest' (impersonal). (2) 'She is said to be honest' (personal passive). Both are grammatically correct passive transformations. Option D uses past tense — wrong (original is present). This is a common exam question testing awareness of dual passive constructions.
